consistency.evidence: adjacent frames leave 4.7% of pixels changed after a global translation, and 0.0% of 24px blocks still differ (worst window 0.3%) -- one rigid scene accounts for the change

matching.reason: retrieval matching against 24 keyframes costs 2364 pairs against 6105 exhaustive (38.7%); the sequential window alone would cost 1055 pairs and find no revisits
unmatched_notes: sequential matching compares only the 10 nearest temporal neighbours, so any two views more than 10 samples apart are not matched by it; on this walk the largest such gap is 55 samples

retrieval matching compares each frame against 24 keyframes, so a revisit matches only if one of its frames is near a keyframe in appearance; a short revisit in a visually distinct part of the room can still be missed
a loop closure missed here shows up as two disconnected reconstructions, not as a bad one: check the registration report before treating a sparse model as a single room

findings.measured: median global translation explains 25% of the frame change
findings.cause: the picture changes without the camera translating, which is a pan, a zoom or a handheld wobble; those give no depth
findings.action: keep translating while turning; translate the camera body, not just the view
